question.text: In a close-ended Category III AIF's Commitment Period, what happens?

answer.text: Investors make one-time lump-sum investments at scheme launch
Investment Manager issues Capital Calls to investors over a pre-defined period (usually first 3 years)
No investments are made; cash is held in treasury

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Close-ended Cat III AIFs operate on a Capital Call model over a Commitment Period, typically the first 3 years of fund tenure. **The Trap:** Lump-sum upfront is not how close-ended structures work; redemption is barred prior to winding-up; cash is invested per strategy. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same drawdown mechanics apply to Cat I/II (XIX-A). **Distributor's Pro-Tip:** Prepare investors for cash flow management across multiple drawdowns — emphasise the 3-year commitment visibility.
